The main takeaway from our work is that
NSAIDs with selective COX‐1 or COX‐2 inhibitory properties may differentially interact with CSA‐induced cardiovascular and autonomic changes in female rats.
COX‐2 inhibitors should be preferred over COX‐1 inhibitors for NSAID co‐treatment with CSA in patients with arthritis.
NSAIDs may have different effects when administered in conjunction with immunosuppressants such as cyclosporine.
